newsitem.title: GABON: Chaos mars Gabon election, voters head home.
newsitem.headline: Chaos mars Gabon election, voters head home.

text.p: Gabon's first multi-party local elections were thrown into chaos on Sunday as people discovered that polling station were unprepared for voters, witnesses said.
Two hours after polls opened officially at 7 a.m. (0600 GMT), many people headed back home without voting because most polling stations had no ballot materials.
"Out of 10 polling stations in one district of the capital, voting was taking place in only three, and one of them was next to the presidential palace," said a witness in Libreville.

"Many voters who have been on line at polling stations since six in the morning are heading back home," he said. "There is a heavy security force presence. In some stations soldiers outnumber the voters."

Oil-rich Gabon is staging the municipal elections as a first test of a 1994 deal between the government and the opposition to set its democratic transition back on course and defuse sometimes bloody political rivalry.
More than 12,000 candidates stood for election as councillors or mayors in the nine provinces of the former Central African French colony.
